transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Time: 10:00 - 10:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Acme CTO), Jordan Lee (Acme Lead ML Eng), Maya Chen (Acme SRE)
Shared: benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/sheets/poc-acme-benchmarks (referenced)

Summary:
Quick recap of weekly POC benchmarks comparing Redwood pilot vs baseline provider. Focus on latency (p50/p95), throughput (rps / tokens/sec), and tuning knobs: batching, KV cache, quantization. Agree next steps for isolated H100 run and production traffic sample.

Topics:
- Baseline numbers and current Redwood optimized results
- Mis-match in p95 under tail traffic
- Batching and KV cache config changes to test
- Security docs and infra integration (VPC, peering)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 30-45 minutes. Samir and I will go through the benchmark sheet, then open floor for questions. Priya, Jordan, Maya, you good on time?
[00:14] Priya (Acme CTO): yeah good, thanks alex. we got the sheet, saw the high level numbers.
[00:23] Samir (Redwood SE): cool, so quick context — we ran parallel benchmarks against your baseline provider (listed as BaselineCloud in the sheet) using your sample workload from last week. tests were on small 4k-token prompts and a 512 token average case. I'll go through p50/p95 and throughput.
[00:40] Jordan (Acme): small note, our prod average seq length is closer to 600, some peaks to 1k depending on summarization jobs.
[00:51] Samir: noted, we used both 512 and 800 traces — the sheet shows both. ok first table, Redwood pilot on H100 with batch 4, kv-cache enabled, quantized int8 path:
[01:05] Samir: p50 token latency 12ms, p95 78ms, throughput 120 rps, tokens/sec ~9.6k at steady state. baseline provider p50 ~18ms, p95 140ms, throughput 85 rps. so overall we're seeing about 40% better throughput and lower tail latency.
[01:33] Priya: those numbers look promising but p95 78ms still spikes sometimes in our production traces. is tail driven by cold KV cache or batching?
[01:42] Samir: good question. the p95 is mostly cold-LM cache misses and occasional GPU context switches under burst. We saw that enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts drops p95 down to ~50ms in the 512 test.
[01:58] Maya (Acme SRE): are you sure caching won't cause data residue concerns? we need to confirm encryption + eviction policies.
[02:06] Alex: yes we have per-customer cache segregation and eviction policies; Samir will attach the cache docs. also note in Dedicated/private setups KV can be customer-managed.
[02:17] Jordan: baseline provider numbers — are they from their A100 instances? i think their sheet says A100-80GB.
[02:24] Samir: baseline was A100-80GB, yes; our Redwood pilot run used H100 with newer kernels and some attention optimizations. that explains some of the delta.
[02:36] Priya: i thought H100 vs A100 might be unfair, can you re-run on A100 so apples-to-apples?
[02:43] Samir: yes we can replicate on A100. action: re-run same batch configs on A100 and share by next week. note though some of our kernel-level ops are tuned for H100 so we may see smaller gains but still expect improved batching and kv cache performance.
[02:59] Alex: also worth remembering we have routing and fallback policies if a customer wants Dedicated vs Hosted, but for this POC you're evaluating Hosted pilot numbers.
[03:10] Jordan: about batching — i saw batch=4 in your run. have you tried batch=8? our traffic peaks usually allow short batching windows.
[03:18] Samir: we ran batch 8 in a separate column — p50 improved to 9ms but p95 increased slightly to 90ms due to queueing under burst patterns. so it's a tradeoff: better throughput, slightly worse tail for some workloads.
[03:34] Maya: can you quantify token/sec change at batch 8?
[03:39] Samir: tokens/sec hit ~14k steady with batch 8 on H100. baseline at batch 8 was 9.2k.
[03:45] Priya: what about quantization — is int8 affecting quality for our summarization prompts? we have strict quality targets.
[03:52] Samir: we ran quality evals — we saw negligible delta on Rouge/qa metrics for int8 for your model family. full eval details are in the "quality" tab. there's a small word-choice drift in a few edge cases, we'll flag examples.
[04:07] Jordan: were there any hallucination regressions?
[04:10] Samir: nothing significant in the sample set, but we recommend running your evaluation prompts — we can run a focused quality regression across your 200 prompt set.
[04:20] Priya: ok please run that.
[04:23] Alex: Samir will run the re-eval and include mention of any prompts with drift.
[04:28] Samir: noted — scheduled.
[04:32] [05:00] Alex: jumping to the p95 under tail — we noticed baseline had worse p95 in cold cache scenarios, but when baseline warmed up with steady traffic their p95 improved. your concern was tail under spiky traffic.
[05:18] Priya: yes spikes are our main issue, we do bursts around 11am daily and monthly batch jobs that cause troughs and spikes. what mitigations can you suggest?
[05:29] Samir: options: 1) pre-warm KV cache for known prefixes; 2) configure autoscale with burst capacity to add Dedicated nodes; 3) use shorter batching windows for latency-sensitive endpoints. each has cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:42] Jordan: can autoscale react in <30s for bursts? we need near-instant for some endpoints.
[05:48] Samir: default autoscale has ~60-90s spinup for Dedicated GPUs, but we offer burst pools that are kept warm and can be used sub-10s. that's an add-on and pricing tradeoff. it's in the sheet under "cost knobs."
[06:02] Maya: about security — priya wants SOC2 + network diagram and the VPC peering steps.
[06:09] Alex: i'll send SOC2 summary and the network diagram after the call. we also support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.
[06:18] Priya: if we go to Private / on-prem for some regulated workloads, how different is the operational burden?
[06:25] Samir: Private requires more infra from your side i.e., k8s or VM fleet, but we ship a package and support install. latency-wise it's similar; main differences are management and updates. we can scope a dedicated onboarding runbook.
[06:38] Jordan: on telemetry — we need trace-level latency per-token breakdown and token-level cost. does Redwood provide that out of the box?
[06:45] Samir: yes in the Console we have per-route and per-token breakdowns, and we can instrument request-level traces. we hooked up a sample trace in the sheet — note some names were mangled by auto transcript — called "token-trace-1".
[06:58] [07:15] Priya: any red flags in the benchmarks?
[07:18] Samir: nothing that prevents pilot continuation; main items are re-running on A100 for parity, and re-checking batch 8 p95 behavior under your exact traffic shape.
[07:26] Alex: ok let's capture exact next steps.
[07:30] Jordan: one more thing — pricing. how much more are we talking if we enable burst warm pools vs just hosted?
[07:36] Alex: we'll send a pricing estimate after we finalize the representative traffic profile. rough order: burst pools add ~15-25% to unit costs vs baseline hosted depending on utilization. i'll get numbers into the sheet.
[07:49] Maya: do we have any compliance checklist for health data specifically?
[07:53] Samir: we have HIPAA-ish guidance and can sign a BAA; i'll pull the compliance pack and send with SOC2.
[07:59] [08:15] Priya: thanks — looks like action items are clear. when's the next sync? same time next week?
[08:21] Alex: yes next Tuesday 10am UTC, i'll send calendar invite.
[08:26] Samir: quick note on the numbers: there's some transcription inconsistency in the sheet where "Redwood Dedicated" was shown as "Redwood Dedicate" — ignore that, it's a typo.
[08:36] Jordan: haha noted.
[08:40] [09:00] Alex: any blockers we didn't cover?
[09:03] Priya: just the A100 parity run and SOC2 docs — otherwise good.
[09:08] Alex: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with updated sheet and docs.
